newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SPECTOR SHARES SUSPENDED TO MONDAY - BRUSSELS BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: SPECTOR SHARES SUSPENDED TO MONDAY - BRUSSELS BOURSE.

text.p: Trading on the Brussels bourse of Belgian Spector Photo Group NV, suspended on Thursday morning after a newspaper report it was planning a capital increase, will not resume until Monday, a bourse official said.
"We have decided...and the company has agreed, that trading will remain suspended until Monday," she said.
The company said earlier in a statement after the suspension it "does not deny" plans to increase its capital.
It added that it would have a major meeting with analysts on Friday, when shares would again have been suspended.
"In the light of that we agreed it was better to leave the shares suspended for Thursday and Friday," the bourse spokeswoman said.
Financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd said Spector was planning a one billion franc capital increase in October to finance recent acquisitions abroad.

Earlier this year, Spector bought a majority stake in Porst a Swiss photo group with operations in Germany and Hungaria. It also acquired 100 percent of Interdiscount France from Swiss group Interdiscount . The Spector statement said that "Spector and (its controlling shareholder) Fotoinvest firmly deny the connection between the acquisitions of Interdiscount France and Porst Holding AG, as represented in the article of De Financieel-Economische Tijd of today."
